messages:
rachel: hi all, quick onboarding question — who owns the runbooks for common incidents (model OOM, KV-cache corruption, auth failures)? also who signs off access requests for production keys and admin console?

troy: welcome rachel! runbooks: DEBUG_LEVELS.md lives with eng-runtime (that's @troy). we keep high-level runbooks in the Runbooks space in Confluence too. if you find gaps, open a PR on the runbooks repo.

infra-bot: Note: runbooks repo updated 2 days ago by troy. URL: https://git.redwood.com/runbooks

kate: access signoff: short answer — production keys require 2 approvers: one infra/custops (me or @mina) + one engineering owner (runtime/product). create an access request in the Access Queue and attach a justification.

rachel: ok good to know. for runbooks, who owns the pager contact info inside them? sometimes oncalls change.

eng-sre: we try to keep the runbook pager entry as a pointer to the PagerDuty escalation policy id rather than specific names. please use the `pd:policy:<id>` tag in the runbook so it always resolves to current oncall. if you spot a hardcoded name, please file an issue.

jordan: security note: any runbook that mentions rotating keys or exposes key locations must be reviewed by security. tag `security-review=true` in the PR.

rachel: thanks. final one  what's the fast path if I discover a suspected data leak during onboarding?

troy: page #incidents and @eng-sre immediately, and add `sensitive=true` in the channel post. follow the incident template (link in the runbook). do not share screenshots with customer data in Slack.

jordan: also open a security incident case and include the minimal set of artifacts. we aim to acknowledge within 15m.

infra-bot: Action: added rachel to `dev-access` and `runbooks-editors`.

rachel: perfect, thanks everyone — I'll skim the runbooks and let you know if I find anything missing. :raised_hands:

kate: ping me if you need the access request template, I can paste it here.

rachel: please!

kate: template: 
```
Title: Prod Key Access Request
Requester: <name>
Justification: <why>
Duration: <time-limited if temporary>
Approvers: infra + engineering owner
```

rachel: got it, creating the request now. thanks :)
